name: Zhang Yiming
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2023); Hurun China U40 (2019-2022); Wikidata (2019); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Yiming is the main cofounder of Chinese tech giant ByteDance, best known for its insanely popular app TikTok, which has more than 1 billion users worldwide.
It also has interests in e-commerce, education, gaming and news.
Zhang stepped down as chairman of ByteDance in 2021 after resigning as CEO earlier that year, reportedly under pressure from the Chinese government.

In 2026, the company ceded control of TikTok's U.S. business to a consortium of mostly American investors including Oracle and Silver Lake Management, which allowed the service to keep operating on U.S. soil.

In China, the tech giant is making strides in AI. Its Doubao AI assistant counted 345 million monthly active users and became the country's most popular AI-powered app in the first quarter of 2026, according to intelligence service provider QuestMobile.
forbes_facts: He was a member of the 2013 Forbes China 30 Under 30 List.
Zhang started ByteDance in 2012 in a four-bedroom Beijing apartment.

name: George Kurtz
sec_insider_companies: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (CRWD) - PRESIDENT AND CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: George Kurtz is cofounder and CEO of CrowdStrike, a cloud-based cybersecurity company based in Sunnyvale, California.
Kurtz cofounded the company with Dmitri Alperovitch in 2011and took it public in 2019.
When internal emails from the Democratic National Committee were leaked to the public in 2016, the DNC hired CrowdStrike to investigate the hack.
In July 2024, a bug in a CrowdStrike software updated set off an outage that grounded flights, took media outlets offline and disrupted companies worldwide.
Prior to CrowdStrike, Kurtz started security tech firm Foundstone in 1999, which was acquired by McAfee in 2004.
CrowdStrike recorded $3.95 billion in revenue in the year through January 31, 2025.

name: John Paulson
sec_insider_companies: Bausch Health Companies Inc. (BHC) - Director; Acadian Asset Management Inc. (AAMI) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Bausch & Lomb Corp (BLCO) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2016); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John Paulson made his fortune betting against subprime mortgages at the peak of the 2007 credit bubble.
His hedge fund firm, Paulson & Co., was started in 1994 and enjoyed success as a niche fund until Paulson put on his "big short" in 2007.
In 2020, Paulson announced that he would be returning capital to investors and converting his hedge fund into a family office.
A Queens native, Paulson had stints at several firms, including Boston Consulting Group and Bear Stearns, before founding Paulson & Co.
Paulson has given $400 million to Harvard University, where he received an MBA, and $100 million to his undergraduate alma mater New York University.

name: Fernando Roberto Moreira Salles
name_chinese: 费尔南多·罗伯托·莫雷拉·萨尔斯
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Fernando Roberto Moreira Salles is a member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
His late father, Walther Moreira Salles, was the founder of Unibanco and a former ambassador to the United States.
In 2008 Unibanco merged with Itau, one of Brazil's-largest commercial banks, creating Itau-Unibanco, the largest private sector bank in Latin America.
Moreira Salles and his three brothers, all billionaires, also own stakes in CBMM, the world's leading supplier of the mineral niobium.
forbes_facts: He owns a stake in the company that controls Companhia das Letras, one of Brazil's largest book publishers.

name: Andrei Guriev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020-2024); Forbes annual (2010-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2018)
forbes_bio: Andrei Guriev is deputy chairman of PhosAgro, one of the world's largest producers of phosphate-based fertilizers.
A former communist committee leader in Moscow, Guriev became deputy director at financial holding company, Menatep Group, in 1990.
When his former boss, Mikhail Khodorkovsky, once Russia's richest person, went to jail, Guriev led a buyout to control Menatep subsidiary PhosAgro.
forbes_facts: Guriev owns Witanhurst estate, which is the second largest in London after Buckingham Palace.
Guriev's son, also Andrei, is CEO of PhosAgro.

name: Peter Thomson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Peter Thomson is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by his grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters; Thomson is on Thomson Reuters' board of directors.
Thomson owns around 14% of the business through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge, where Thomson serves as chairman.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Global and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Mark Meijer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Mark Meijer owns the Michigan-based grocery chain Meijer with his brothers Hank and Doug.
Mark has no role in day-to-day operations but serves on the company's board of directors.
He runs an ambulance company, Life EMS, that he cofounded in 1980.
Meijer has 500 stores in the Midwest and estimated revenues of $22 billion.
His grandfather, Henrik, a Dutch immigrant, started the company in 1934.

name: Johnelle Hunt
sec_insider_companies: HUNT J B TRANSPORT SERVICES INC (JBHT) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: In 1961, Johnelle Hunt and her late husband J.B. (d. 2006) sold their home and took out loans to start a rice hull packaging operation.
Eight years later, the couple bought five trucks and seven trailers to launch trucking firm J.B. Hunt Transport Services.
The Lowell, Arkansas, business went public in 1983 and is now one of the biggest transportation companies in the nation, with $12.1 billion in sales.
Hunt, who stepped down as corporate secretary in 2008, remains the firm's largest individual shareholder, with a 19% stake.

She donated $5 million to the J.B. and Johnelle Hunt Family Ozark Highlands Center, which opened in Springdale, Arkansas in 2020. In 2024, she announced a $100 million gift to the University of Arkansas.
forbes_facts: The daughter of a poultry business owner, Hunt studied to be a teacher at University of Central Arkansas before leaving to marry J.B.
Hunt was a part of the 11 inaugural inductees to the Arkansas Women's Hall of Fame, which opened in 2015.

name: Kevin David Lehmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Kevin David Lehmann owns 50% of Germany's leading drugstore chain, dm (drogerie markt), which brings in over $14 billion in annual revenue.
The company got its start in 1973 when Goetz Werner opened his first shop in Karlsruhe, Germany. Today, dm has some 3,700 locations.
In 1974, Kevin David Lehmann's father, Guenther, then running his family's Pfannkuch grocery chain, invested in dm.
Guenther quietly transferred ownership of his 50% dm stake to Kevin David in 2017.
Neither Kevin David nor his father have been operationally involved in dm. Little is known about them.
forbes_facts: The dm philosophy, that ensuring employee well being brings greater long-term success for the company, is well known in German-speaking countries.
Goetz Werner transferred his 50% of dm to a charitable foundation. His son Christoph, a member of dm's management board since 2011, now manages the company.
